import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality,
# while using Stress Level for color (hue) and Physical Activity Level for point size.
# This allows for observing multi-variate relationships.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability and legend space

scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level', # Color points by Stress Level
    size='Physical Activity Level', # Size points by Physical Activity Level
    sizes=(50, 800), # Range of sizes for the bubbles for better visual distinction
    palette='viridis', # Perceptually uniform colormap for stress level
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for overlapping points
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep: Impact of Stress Level and Physical Activity', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement: Seaborn automatically creates separate legends for hue and size.
# We'll let tight_layout manage their positioning.
# If legends overlap, manual adjustment with plt.legend() and bbox_to_anchor would be needed.

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality,
# while using Stress Level for color (hue) and Physical Activity Level for point size.
# This allows for observing multi-variate relationships.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability and legend space

scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level', # Color points by Stress Level
    size='Physical Activity Level', # Size points by Physical Activity Level
    sizes=(50, 800), # Range of sizes for the bubbles for better visual distinction
    palette='viridis', # Perceptually uniform colormap for stress level
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for overlapping points
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep: Impact of Stress Level and Physical Activity', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement: Seaborn automatically creates separate legends for hue and size.
# We'll let tight_layout manage their positioning.
# If legends overlap, manual adjustment with plt.legend() and bbox_to_anchor would be needed.

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
